title: Longitudinal recovery of the candidate mini2p field of view
scientific_context: Blood and acute optical disturbance can obscure the field of view on the surgery day. Repeated Z-stacks are used to describe how visible tissue and cells extend into deeper planes during recovery before mini2p mounting and later LabGraph experiments.
primary_question: At which post-surgery time point is the candidate field of view sufficiently recovered, including at depth, to support selection of an optimal mini2p mounting location?

analysis_units.reconstruction_unit: one physical Z-stack acquisition, one saved ScanImage channel
analysis_units.independence_rule: Frames and planes are technical observations and must never be counted as independent biological replicates.

longitudinal_design.comparison_order: within-animal trajectory first, animal-balanced summary second

input_boundary.purpose: The pipeline reconstructs the Z-stack itself; raw ScanImage pages and metadata are therefore the required primary input rather than a fallback QC input.
input_boundary.discovery_contract: Browse and resolve data through ResearchDataGovernance or the current LabGraph data-access contract before execution.
input_boundary.write_policy: Source TIFFs are read-only and are never modified.

reconstruction_required: saved channel is unambiguous or explicitly selected
TIFF page count matches ScanImage metadata
Z positions are strictly increasing and match the declared step
longitudinal_comparison_required: animal, acquisition date, scan ID, session ID, and source channel are present
source review flags affecting intensity, background, or depth visibility are resolved or explicitly stratified
eligibility.exclusion_policy: Never silently drop a failed, missing, duplicate, or flagged acquisition; record its disposition and reason.

missing_data_policy: Represent missing days and unavailable surgery dates explicitly. Do not interpolate an unobserved day or treat irregularly sampled days as equally spaced replicates.
statistical_method: Version 0.2.0 performs deterministic per-scan reconstruction and descriptive QC only; it does not estimate an optimal post-surgery day.
planned_outcomes: deepest usable visible plane or contiguous usable depth
mounting-readiness decision with explicit QC evidence
supported_interpretations: The run reconstructs and displays one declared scan and channel under versioned settings.
Descriptive metadata and QC can identify scans that are suitable for later longitudinal comparison.
unsupported_interpretations: The current reconstruction alone identifies the optimal mounting day.
Brightness differences alone prove biological recovery.
Frames or planes are independent biological replicates.

governance.local_adoption_note: ZStackAnalysis owns its runtime code and frozen configuration while adopting the LabGraph run and figure contracts.
